_comment: The Lean-to-manuscript census registry read by tools/lean_manuscript_census.py. Every OIBridge module belongs to exactly one family; every family carries a disposition; a family the manuscripts carry (current, consistent-uncited, scope-consistent) names at least one anchor; a superseded identifier may appear in a manuscript paragraph only alongside its successor. Registry contract (AGENTS.md A.35): the check is complete relative to this file, so every publication-facing strengthening of a theorem inside an existing module updates this file in the same commit, with a supersession entry for the identifier it replaces and an anchor for the statement the manuscripts must now carry.

families.name: representation bridge and counting
families.note: The cubic counting layer of the SM paper (the averaging identity, the equivariant-map dimension formula, dim Hom_G(V6,V6) = 3). The paper states the results in its own derivation, anchored at the link-representation decomposition and its multiplicities; no kernel pointer is placed in SM.md. A pointer pass is an owner decision.

families.name: equivalence chain and memory
families.note: Main 3.4: the finite-horizon equivalence, the memory and necessity theorems, the Weyl-twirl separability results. Main states them with proofs; kernel pointers are not placed. A pointer pass is an owner decision.

families.name: Hamiltonian reconstruction
families.note: GR 3.3: Bohr-frequency completeness, the two-branch D-gauge theorem graded on the cited integer classification, the homometric exception killed, antiunitary invariance, the thermodynamic orientation selector.

families.name: coherent completions
families.note: GR 3.3: lift obstructions, the coherent-completion classification, the orientation no-go. The observability, passive and controlled quotients underwrite no manuscript statement (Audit A, CONCRETE-CUT-FREEZE.md); ControlLie is machinery for the completion classification.

families.name: instruments, dilation and assembly
families.note: The finite operational theory structure, the Stinespring assembly, Kraus soundness, the positive-but-not-completely-positive countermodel and the boundary ledger: machinery consumed by the completion classification. DimensionalCountermodel supplies the witness `countermodel` cited in GR 3.3.

families.name: completion classification and the primitive-source chain

manuscript.anchor: no closure of the implementations under the adjoint
no closure of the implementations under the adjoint

families.note: GR 3.3 (the operational-completion characterization, OI+, the primitive-source form), Main 3.4, the Explainer note, book chapters 1 and 19. The strongest package is OIPlusMin (the minimal-repertoire family); OIPlusPos is stated as the elementary-repertoire form beside it, and the OI+ layered form and the five-condition form as the layered and five-condition forms, not as the strongest package. SubstantiveCensus, CompositionalIndependence and LevelOneRecursion are independence scaffolding cited in the verification notes only.

families.name: substratum source
families.note: GR 3.3 substratum-source form and its boxed endpoint; the endpoint is unchanged by the primitive-source compressions.

families.name: typed completion
families.note: GR 3.3 typed form; the package-level corollary is cited from the current package.

families.name: quasilocal completion
families.note: GR 3.3 infinite-region completion, with its scope (fixed lattice, no continuum limit, no representation selected).

families.name: instrument audit

manuscript.anchor: it is not a characterization of all infinite-dimensional quantum instruments

families.note: The manuscripts carry the scope qualification; the finite-support redundancy result itself is not narrated, and no live corpus claim requires infinite-support interventions (INSTRUMENT-COMPLETION-AUDIT.md).

families.name: continuous time (CT2)

manuscript.anchor: What the substratum does determine is a path
A continuous-time Hamiltonian law is additional structure
not a one-parameter group and exhibiting no generator
not a one-parameter group and exhibiting no generator

families.note: GR 3.3, continuous-time paragraph: the depth-two factorization, the two layer groups, and the norm-continuous path of local *-automorphisms from the identity to the update's Heisenberg action, stated as a path and not a one-parameter group, with no generator exhibited and CT3 open; Main 2.3 and the quasilocal summaries in Main 3.4, the Explainer and the book chapters carry the same. A continuous-time Hamiltonian law stays additional structure.

families.name: minimal repertoire
families.note: The elementary repertoire cut to one continuously driven pair and the exchanges, with no quarter phase (OIPlusMin, carrier_general_oiPlusMin, the bipartite obstruction). GR 3.3 states phase-free richness as the second primitive-source principle with the elementary repertoire as its stronger form; Main 3.4, the Explainer and the book chapters carry the summary. The cycle claim is stated at its evidence: the even-carrier countercontrol is cited, no iff over D and no minimality of the driven transition is asserted.

families.name: OI-N passive observation
families.note: The frozen exploratory thread (OI-N-FREEZE.md): noncommutativity forbids complete passive observation; passive incompleteness does not diagnose OICore; a passive internal observer only reads an existing record; a new internal record changes the joint system. Not narrated in the manuscripts; the freeze note says it is citable only for what its modules prove. Adding it is an owner decision, and no manuscript sentence contradicts it.
